payout_quote: Federal jurors are paid $50 a day. After 10 days on a petit jury (if the judge orders it) or 45 days on a grand jury, the rate may rise to $60 a day. Federal employees receive salary instead of the fee.
steps: Report and serve on a petit or grand jury
Receive $50/day attendance fee (up to $60/day after 10 petit-jury days if ordered, or 45 grand-jury days)
catches: You cannot volunteer — service is by random summons only.
Federal government employees get their salary instead of the juror fee (no extra pay).
The $60 rate is not automatic; it requires a judge's order (petit) or 45 days (grand jury).
biggest_catch: You can't sign up — federal jury service is summons-only, and federal employees get no extra fee at all.
eligibility: US citizens summoned for federal jury service (random selection from voter/DMV lists).
timing: Paid for each day of service; extended-service rate per court order.
